Published online:
    September 11, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Europe (primary), US, Middle East

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    European equities posted modest Friday gains but faced their worst weekly drop in ~two months, pressured by surging bond yields, ECB rate hike warnings, and oil prices back above $100/bbl driven by escalating US-Iran military conflict in the Middle East. Market focus centers on incoming US CPI data and the upcoming Fed meeting, with traders pricing a 67% probability of a Fed rate hike. The ECB has already moved, flagging persistent inflation from energy price shocks. Individual movers: Technoprobe +3.6% (TSMC revenue tailwind), FlatexDEGIRO -4.9% (chairman resignation).

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES — US CPI, Fed rate path, and Treasury yields are central drivers of the narrative, though framed through the lens of European market impact.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 80 (moderately-high — rate hike probability and hawkish Fed expectations are a key theme)
Probability of increase: 67% (explicitly cited via CME FedWatch)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 20 (minor — holding is implicitly the alternative but not the article's focus)
Probability of holding: 33% (implied residual from the 67% hike probability)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (NO — no mention of cuts; context is entirely hawkish)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 70 (Hawkish — 67% market-implied hike probability, 10Y yields pressing toward 5%, persistent inflation from oil shock, and Fed meeting imminent all point clearly in a tightening direction with no dovish offsets mentioned)
